name: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
desc: Roman-style spaghetti tossed with crisp guanciale, whole eggs and yolks, pecorino, Parmesan, and plenty of black pepper.

source.title: Carbonara (Ian Fisher)
source.evidence: Identical amounts (12 oz spaghetti, 2 eggs plus 2 yolks, 1 oz each pecorino and Parmesan, 3 1/2 oz guanciale, pancetta or bacon, 1 tbsp olive oil) and the same method: pasta a bit firmer than al dente, 1 cup pasta water reserved, sauce finished in a warmed serving bowl.

ingredients.raw: 2 large eggs plus 2 large yolks, at room temperature
1 oz finely grated pecorino Romano (about 1/3 packed cup), plus more for serving
ingredients.note: about 1/3 packed cup, plus more for serving

ingredients.raw: 1 oz finely grated Parmesan (about 1/3 packed cup)
Coarsely ground black pepper, generously, plus more for serving
3 1/2 oz guanciale, pancetta, or thick-cut bacon, cut into 1/4-inch-thick pieces
Kosher salt (no more than 1 tbsp for the pasta water, plus a pinch for the eggs)

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with no more than 1 tbsp salt. Fill a large serving bowl with hot tap water to warm it.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs, yolks, pecorino, and Parmesan. Season with a pinch of salt and a generous amount of black pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the guanciale and cook, stirring, until the fat renders and the edges are on the edge of crisp but not hard, 5-7 min. Take off the heat.
Cook the spaghetti until a bit firmer than al dente (about 1 min less than the package says). Just before it is ready, rewarm the guanciale if it has cooled.
Scoop out 1 cup pasta water, then drain the pasta and add it to the skillet over low heat. Toss for about 1 min to coat in the fat.

Empty and dry the warmed serving bowl and tip in the pasta and guanciale. Pour in the egg mixture and toss quickly, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce turns creamy and clings to the strands.
Serve immediately with more pecorino and black pepper.
tips: Mix the eggs in off the heat, in the warmed bowl, so they thicken into a sauce instead of scrambling. The hot pasta cooks them.

references.title: Carbonara
